Rub the duck inside and out with the dry cure; leave uncovered on a rack 12 h at 0–4 °C.
Rinse off the cure lightly and pat completely dry.
Fill the cavity with orange and shallot; truss the legs and tuck the wings.
Brush with soy sauce mixed with oil; set on a rack over a tray with the water.
Roast breast up at 160 °C convection for 1 h.
Pour off the fat, turn breast down and roast 30 min at 170 °C.
Turn breast up, brush with the glaze and roast 30 min at 190 °C until the skin is crisp and deep golden; core 75 °C in the thigh.
Reduce the wine with the honey by half; stir in the balsamic.
Brush over the duck during the final 30 min of roasting.
Serve a quarter duck (breast or leg), ≈ 300 g with bone, brushed with the remaining glaze.

Dice sweet potato 2 cm; toss with half the oil, spices and salt; roast 210 °C 22–25 min.
Toss drained chickpeas with the rest of the oil; roast 15 min until crisp.
Whisk tahini, lemon, garlic and water to a pourable dressing; season.

Cut all vegetables into 12 mm dice.
Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the olive oil for 6–8 min without colour. Add the pepper and courgette and cook 3 min.
Add the garlic for 30 s, then take off the heat, add the paprika and cumin and stir 30 s to bloom.
Add the tomatoes, stock and chickpeas. Simmer 20 min until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Season with the salt and pepper; finish with the parsley. Serve at ≥75 °C.

Add the tomato paste and garlic; cook 2 min.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, stock, thyme and bay leaf; bring to the boil.
Simmer gently 35–40 min, stirring now and then, until the lentils are tender and the ragù is thick.
Remove the bay leaf; season with the salt. Serve at ≥ 63 °C.

Season with soy sauce and salt; spread in a GN.
Boil potatoes and sweet potatoes 20–25 min; drain, mash with oil, nutmeg and salt (use some cooking water).
Spread over the lentils; mark with a fork.

Return mushrooms, add stock, simmer 5 min; stir in mustard.
Off the boil, stir in sour cream (do not boil after); season with lemon, salt and pepper; finish with parsley.

Sweat onion, grated carrot and zucchini flesh in oil 8 min; add washed rice, paprika and tomato paste, fry 2 min.

Fill zucchini halves; place in an oiled GN.
Pour hot stock around; cover with foil and bake 180 °C 35 min; uncover 10 min.

Pan-fry in oil 6–8 min until golden on all sides (or 220 °C oven 20 min).
Simmer soy, mirin, sugar, ginger and garlic 4 min; toss tofu in the glaze 1 min.
Rinse rice; cook covered 12 min; rest 10 min.
Steam broccoli florets and edamame 3–4 min; julienne carrot; pickle cucumber slices in rice vinegar 10 min.

Quarter the mushrooms; cut the aubergine and courgette into 25 mm cubes and the pepper into 20 mm strips.
Salt the aubergine for 20 min, rinse and dry. Toss with 5 g of the oil and roast in a convection oven at 200 °C for 12–15 min until coloured.
Sear the mushrooms in a hot dry pan until well coloured, then add 5 g of the oil.
In a second pan sweat the onion in the remaining oil; add the pepper and courgette for 4–5 min, then the garlic for 30 s.
Take off the heat and stir in the paprika (prevents scorching).
Add the mushrooms, aubergine, tomatoes and stock; simmer for 15 min.
Season with the salt and pepper; finish with the savoury. Serve at ≥75 °C.
Boil the potatoes in unsalted water until tender, 15–20 min. Drain.
Plate ≈260 g kavarma with ≈125 g potatoes; finish with the parsley.
